deck: This week, smaller launch providers and AI startups made notable moves.

stories.head: HyImpulse eyes Oman’s launch potential.
stories.body: HyImpulse has signed a letter of intent with Oman’s Etlaq Spaceport to explore launch activities, marking a notable step for small launch providers. This move indicates that even the smallest players are keen to stake their claim in the global launch market, which is increasingly competitive. Oman’s strategic location could provide a unique advantage for future launches.
stories.soWhat: If small players can access international markets, the launch landscape could become even more fragmented—and chaotic.

stories.head: Tilebox launches AI workflows—robots don’t lie?
stories.body: Tilebox has rolled out new verifiable AI workflows for satellite data, aiming to enhance trust in automated processes. While the technology sounds impressive, it raises the question of whether these safeguards are more about optics than actual innovation. The satellite data market is increasingly reliant on AI, making this move part of a broader trend.
stories.soWhat: If AI verification becomes the norm, expect a flood of similar offerings, but the real question will be who can actually deliver on the promises.

stories.head: K2 Space and Rocket Lab win Space Force contracts.
stories.body: K2 Space and Rocket Lab have secured key supplier roles in the Space Force's satellite communications program, with K2 landing $110 million in Series B funding for its megaclass satellite bus. The military’s demand for satellite buses continues to grow, reflecting an insatiable appetite for enhanced communication capabilities. This trend underscores the ongoing shift towards commercial partnerships in defense.
stories.soWhat: As the military leans more on commercial capabilities, expect an uptick in defense contracts for those who can deliver.

watchlist.title: True Anomaly's next steps after $190M raise.
watchlist.body: With a fresh $190 million, True Anomaly will likely ramp up its co-orbital security initiatives, making it a player to watch in the defense sector.

watchlist.title: Implications of FY27 budget boost.
watchlist.body: The $1.4 billion increase for space resilience could signal a shift in government priorities, potentially leading to more contracts for resilient space technologies.

watchlist.title: Sierra Space's Dream Chaser readiness.
watchlist.body: With its DoD variant clearing design review, the next milestone will be its actual flight, which could set a precedent for future military space transport.

watchlist.title: Founders Fund's space portfolio review.
watchlist.body: As Founders Fund reassesses its investments, any pivots could signal broader trends in venture capital's appetite for space startups.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
